context: Reverse osmosis (RO) desalination plants force saline water under high hydraulic pressure through semi-permeable polymeric membranes that retain dissolved salts and impurities while allowing water molecules to pass. Modern high-recovery RO systems pair semi-permeable membranes with energy recovery devices that capture pressure energy from the concentrated brine stream to reduce specific electricity demand. Nonetheless, membrane fouling from organic matter and mineral scaling still requires periodic pretreatment, chemical cleaning, and careful brine management to protect marine ecosystems.
